Inside the doors

Two walls of machines, and a reader that takes your phone.

It’s all self-serve — you load, you pay at the machine, you come back for it. Tap a heading to see what’s actually on the floor.

  • Front-load Speed QueensA long row of them down one wall, with a basket shelf running above.
  • The double-wide machinesThe tall ones at the end of the row — the panel marks their capacity with six baskets in a line.
  • Set it on the panelSoil: light, medium or heavy. Cycle: normal, perm press or delicates. Temperature: hot, warm or cold. Bleach has its own dispenser.
  • Numbered so you can find yoursN3, N4, N5 and up the wall — the number is stencilled on every door.
  • Minutes on the frontEach stack has a lit display over the door counting down what’s left, so you can see from across the room.
  • Newer stacks, newer readersThe stainless bank at the back runs on touchscreens instead of a keypad.
  • Card at the machineThe reader on the front is marked “Payments made easy” — Visa, Mastercard and Discover.
  • Or just your phoneApple Pay and Google Pay are printed on the same reader.
  • Coins or cardStep five on the washer panel reads “Insert Coins/Card”, and the older dryer stacks still have a slot marked 25¢.
  • No animal blanketsPosted over the dryer stacks.
  • Don’t leave a load sitting“We reserve the right to remove unattended laundry from machines to enable new customer use.”
  • Not responsible for lost, damaged or stolen itemsOn the wall by the dryers.
  • Video surveillanceA camera on the corner of the building and a notice on the glass — worth knowing for a late load.

The place

No counter, nobody to wait on.

Buckley Laundromat is a self-serve room on Highway 410 — you run your own load from start to finish.

There’s no attendant standing behind a desk. As one regular put it in her review, there’s no employee on the premises except for opening and closing, and select days set aside for cleaning and repairs. The rest of the day the room is yours.

You’ll know the building from the highway: a blue standing-seam roof, cedar posts either side of the door, river rock around the base, and the rainbow bubble sign across the top of the glass. The address is right there on the window — 393A HWY 410 E.

“We are here to serve the community.”Their Facebook page

Something wrong with a machine?

Nobody’s at a counter — so tell them here.

  1. Say which machine

    The number is on the front of every one — N4, N7, 2-6. That’s the fastest way to get it looked at.

  2. Say when you were in

    The day and roughly the time, since there’s no one on the floor to have seen it.

  3. Leave a number

    They’ll come back to you directly.
